name: Timon
overview: Timon was a male figure in the early Christian community, notably chosen to serve the widows of the Hellenistic Jews. His role highlights the practical care and organization within the early church, addressing the needs of vulnerable members. No further tribal or familial details are recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Timon appears in the New Testament without a given meaning or divine origin. It is presented simply as a proper name in Acts 6:5, identifying this individual without additional title or descriptive meaning.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Timon beyond his service role mentioned in Acts 6:5. There are no known relatives or connections detailed in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Timon's significance lies in his selection as one of the seven men appointed to serve the widows among the Hellenistic Jewish believers. This appointment reflects the early church's commitment to orderly ministry and compassionate care, ensuring that the needs of all members were met. His role exemplifies faithful service and the practical outworking of the gospel in community life.
